key_insight: Model class prototypes as time-aware trajectories and learn a low-curvature prototype flow to constrain their evolution, which reduces representation drift and mitigates catastrophic forgetting in class-incremental remote sensing segmentation.
problem_solved: Addresses forgetting and representation drift when segmentation models are updated incrementally with new classes and shifting acquisition conditions (seasons, cities, sensors).
method: Represent class prototypes as trajectories in feature space and track their temporal evolution across incremental steps.
Learn a prototype flow with a low-curvature regularizer and temporal-consistency objectives to enforce smooth, stable prototype transitions.
Integrate the prototype-flow module into class-incremental segmentation training to constrain representation drift and preserve prior knowledge.
impact: Provides a practical mechanism to retain prior segmentation knowledge while adapting to new classes and domain shifts, improving robustness and lowering maintenance cost for deployed remote sensing systems.
visual_elements: 2D embedding of prototype trajectories over time: low-curvature (smooth) vs high-curvature (drift) examples

paper_title: ProtoFlow: Mitigating Forgetting in Class-Incremental Remote Sensing Segmentation via Low-Curvature Prototype Flow
paper_authors: Jiekai Wu, Rong Fu, Chuangqi Li, Zijian Zhang, Guangxin Wu
